chapters.title: Chapter 4: Choosing the Right ITR Form

lessons.title: When You Need ITR-2 or ITR-3: Capital Gains, Foreign Assets and Freelance Income

body.text: ITR-2 and ITR-3 are not harder because the tax is harder. They are harder because they make you show your working: every gain, every foreign holding and every rupee of trading turnover gets its own schedule.

markDefs.definition: A section of an ITR form dedicated to one type of income, asset or tax detail, such as Schedule CG for capital gains or Schedule FA for foreign assets. ITR-2 and ITR-3 have many more schedules than ITR-1.

children.text: Lesson 1 of this chapter told you when you land in ITR-2 or ITR-3. This lesson shows what those forms then ask of you. Each is built from

, and the portal only opens the ones relevant to the income you declare. Knowing which schedules you will face, and what data each needs, tells you exactly which statements to download before you start.

body.title: ITR-2 vs ITR-3: What Each Adds

columns.label: ITR-2: No Business Income
points: Schedule CG and Schedule 112A for capital gains of any size
Schedule VDA for crypto and other virtual digital assets
Schedule FA for foreign assets, and Schedules FSI and TR for foreign income and tax credit
Schedule AL for assets and liabilities if total income exceeds ₹1 crore

columns.label: ITR-3: With Business or Profession
points: Schedule BP to compute business or professional income
Profit and loss account and balance sheet details where books are kept
Trading turnover for F&O and intraday
Presumptive income under Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (44AD and 44ADA of the 1961 Act) when ITR-4 is not available

children.text: Capital Gains: Schedule CG and Schedule 112A

Schedule CG is where every capital gain and loss is computed and set off. Long-term gains on listed equity shares and equity mutual funds are first detailed in Schedule 112A and then flow into Schedule CG. For FY 2025-26, the form no longer needs you to split transactions before and after 23 July 2024, because every sale in the year falls under the current rates. Your broker's tax P&L and your CAMS or KFintech capital gains statement give you almost everything you need.

body.caption: Where Each Type of Gain Goes, FY 2025-26

cells: Listed shares and equity mutual funds, held 12 months or less
Listed shares and equity mutual funds, held over 12 months
12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh under Section 198 (112A of the 1961 Act)
Debt mutual funds bought on or after 1 April 2023
Slab rates, whatever the holding period
Property, gold, unlisted and foreign shares
Slab rates if held 24 months or less
Crypto and other virtual digital assets
30% flat; losses cannot be set off against any other income

children.text: Neha, a marketing manager in Pune whose salary already uses up her basic exemption limit, invests through Groww. In FY 2025-26 she booked a ₹60,000 short-term gain on one stock, a ₹25,000 short-term loss on another, and a ₹2,05,000 long-term gain on equity mutual funds.

body.caption: Neha's Capital Gains in Schedule CG

body.title: Total Neha's Capital Gains Tax
body.prompt: Using the table above, what is Neha's total tax on her capital gains, including 4% cess?
body.explanation: ₹7,000 on short-term gains plus ₹10,000 on long-term gains is ₹17,000. Adding 4% cess of ₹680 gives ₹17,680. Notice where the short-term loss was used. Set against the short-term gain it saves 20%, or ₹5,000. Set against the long-term gain above the exemption it would save only 12.5%, or ₹3,125. A short-term loss can offset either type of gain, so always check how the set-off has been applied.

body.text: Schedule 112A looks intimidating, but share-by-share detail is required only for shares and units bought on or before 31 January 2018, where grandfathering of cost applies. For everything bought later, the gains can be reported in consolidated form. Most brokers and registrars now give a Schedule 112A-ready report you can upload.

children.text: Foreign Assets: Schedule FA, FSI and TR

If you are a resident and held any asset outside India, Schedule FA must list it, even if it earned nothing. That includes US stocks bought through apps like Vested or INDmoney, RSUs and ESPP shares from a multinational employer, and bank accounts abroad. Two schedules handle the income: Schedule FSI reports income earned abroad, such as dividends on US shares, and Schedule TR claims credit for tax already paid in the other country.

body.caption: Foreign Asset Reporting Essentials for AY 2026-27

cells: Schedule FA covers the calendar year, 1 January to 31 December 2025, not the financial year
Typically the initial value, peak value during the period, closing value, and income or sale proceeds, converted to rupees as the ITR instructions specify
File Form 67 on the portal before filing your ITR, then claim the credit in Schedules FSI and TR
The credit cannot exceed the Indian tax payable on that foreign income
Failing to disclose foreign assets can attract a penalty of ₹10 lakh under the Black Money Act

body.title: The Calendar Year Twist
body.question: Vikram, an engineer in Hyderabad, files ITR-2 for FY 2025-26. He bought US shares in March 2025 and more in February 2026. For Schedule FA in this return, which period does he report?
options: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, the financial year
1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, the calendar year
Only the dates on which he actually bought shares
body.explanation: Schedule FA for residents follows the calendar year ending during the financial year, so this return covers January to December 2025. His March 2025 purchase is reported now. The February 2026 purchase falls in calendar year 2026 and will appear in next year's Schedule FA. Any dividends or sale gains, though, are still taxed in the financial year they arise.

body.text: Foreign dividends are usually taxed twice before you get a credit. US companies withhold tax on dividends paid to Indian residents, and India taxes the same dividend at your slab rate. You can claim credit for the US tax, but only if Form 67 is filed before your return. File the ITR first and you may lose the credit.

children.text: In ITR-3, business and professional income is computed in Schedule BP. A freelancer or consultant can report it in one of two ways: actual profit, backed by a profit and loss account and balance sheet, or presumptive income under Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Sections 44AD and 44ADA of the 1961 Act). A freelancer who would have used ITR-4 but also has short-term capital gains or foreign assets still uses the presumptive scheme, just inside ITR-3.

markDefs.definition: For F&O trading, the sum of the absolute values of profits and losses on each trade, as per the ICAI Guidance Note. It is used to test tax audit requirements, not to compute tax.

children.text: . It is not the contract value of your trades and not your net profit. You add up the profit or loss on every trade, ignoring whether it was a profit or a loss. Turnover decides whether a tax audit is needed; tax is still charged only on your net profit.

body.latex: \text{F\&O Turnover} = \sum \left| \text{Profit or Loss on Each Trade} \right|
body.caption: Option premium is no longer added separately under the revised ICAI Guidance Note, as it is already reflected in each trade's profit or loss.

body.title: Compute the F&O Turnover
body.prompt: Sameer, a salaried analyst in Mumbai, closed five Nifty options trades on Zerodha in FY 2025-26 with these results: profit ₹45,000, loss ₹30,000, profit ₹12,000, loss ₹58,000, profit ₹9,000. What is his F&O turnover for the year?
body.explanation: Add the absolute values: ₹45,000 + ₹30,000 + ₹12,000 + ₹58,000 + ₹9,000 = ₹1,54,000. His net result is a loss of ₹22,000 (₹66,000 of profits minus ₹88,000 of losses). He reports ₹1,54,000 as turnover and a ₹22,000 business loss in ITR-3, filed by the due date so the loss can be carried forward.

body.label: Tax Audit Threshold for Traders
body.context: Applies when cash receipts and payments are within 5% of the total, which is the norm for exchange-traded F&O. Under the Income-tax Act, 1961 this is Section 44AB. Traders who have opted for presumptive taxation can face an audit at much lower levels if they declare profits below the presumptive rate, so take professional advice in that situation.

cards.definition: Computes all short-term and long-term capital gains and losses, and their set-off.
Details long-term gains on listed equity and equity funds; share-by-share only for holdings bought on or before 31 January 2018.
Reports gains on crypto and other virtual digital assets, taxed at a flat 30%.
Lists foreign assets held by a resident during the calendar year.
Reports income earned outside India, such as US dividends.
Claims credit for tax paid abroad, supported by Form 67 filed before the return.
Lists assets and liabilities at year end, required only when total income exceeds ₹1 crore.
ITR-3 only. Computes income from business or profession, including F&O and presumptive income.

body.title: The Freelancer With Everything
body.scenario: Aditi, 32, is a freelance UI designer in Kolkata working for clients in the US and Europe, paid into her Indian bank account. Her gross receipts for FY 2025-26 are ₹28,00,000, all by bank transfer, and she wants to use the presumptive scheme for professionals. In 2023 she bought US shares through an investing app and sold some of them in October 2025 at a gain. She also redeemed an Indian equity mutual fund held for seven months, booking a short-term gain. Her total income is well below ₹1 crore.
body.prompt: Which ITR form does Aditi file, and which schedules will she need to fill? Explain what goes into each.
body.modelAnswer: Aditi files ITR-3. Her professional income on its own would fit ITR-4, but ITR-4 cannot hold short-term capital gains or foreign assets. Inside ITR-3: Schedule BP carries her presumptive professional income under Section 58 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (44ADA of the 1961 Act), at least 50% of ₹28,00,000, so ₹14,00,000 or more. Schedule CG carries two gains. The US shares are foreign shares, not listed in India, so held for over 24 months they are long-term, taxed at 12.5% without the ₹1.25 lakh equity exemption. The mutual fund redemption, held seven months, is a short-term gain on an equity fund, taxed at 20%. Schedule FA must list her US shareholding for calendar year 2025, including the October 2025 sale proceeds. Schedules FSI and TR are needed only if she earned foreign income with foreign tax deducted, such as US dividends; capital gains on US shares are generally not taxed in the US for her, so there may be no credit to claim. Schedule AL is not required, as her income is below ₹1 crore. Since she has business income, her due date is 31 August 2026.

body.title: Before You Open ITR-2 or ITR-3
steps: Download your broker's tax P&L and a Schedule 112A-ready report
Download your CAMS, KFintech or MF Central capital gains statement
Pull statements from any foreign broker or employer stock plan for calendar year 2025
If you received foreign dividends with tax withheld, file Form 67 before the ITR
Traders: compute F&O and intraday turnover trade by trade, and note net profit or loss
Freelancers: decide between actual profit with books and the presumptive scheme
If total income exceeds ₹1 crore, list your assets and liabilities as on 31 March 2026 for Schedule AL
Note your due date: 31 July 2026 for ITR-2, 31 August 2026 for non-audit ITR-3

points: ITR-2 adds Schedules CG, 112A, VDA, FA, FSI, TR and AL to ITR-1; ITR-3 adds Schedule BP and business accounts on top of ITR-2
Capital gains are computed in Schedule CG, with listed equity taxed at 20% short-term under Section 196 and 12.5% long-term above ₹1.25 lakh under Section 198
Schedule 112A needs share-by-share detail only for holdings bought on or before 31 January 2018; crypto goes in Schedule VDA at a flat 30%
Schedule FA covers foreign assets held during calendar year 2025, and foreign tax credit needs Form 67 filed before the ITR
F&O turnover is the sum of absolute profits and losses on each trade; it tests audit applicability, while tax is on net profit
Freelancers disqualified from ITR-4 can still use presumptive income under Section 58 inside ITR-3, and Schedule AL applies only above ₹1 crore of income

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. Foreign asset reporting, foreign tax credit, trading turnover and tax audit rules involve significant nuance, and schedules and thresholds reflect the AY 2026-27 forms at the time of writing. Consult a qualified tax professional for foreign income, F&O trading or business income, and verify requirements on the Income Tax Department's portal.
